We need to apply template 1914391 to the target molecule. The target molecule is likely the product from previous step? The earlier input from make_5_lvl1-apply_template-4 gave precursors list: ["CCOC(C[C@@H]1O[C@H](/C=C(/C)C(OC)=O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)CH2)=O", "O=S(=O)(O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C(F)(F)F"] That seems unrelated.

Now we have template 1914391 and mapped_rxn. We need to apply to the molecule given in the task? The task says: "return all possible precursors of applying the template as the result of the task make_5_lvl1-template_search-5 to the molecule below". The molecule below? Not explicitly given but likely the same as earlier? The previous apply_template-4 used molecule "CCOC(C[C@@H]1O[C@H](/C=C(/C)C(OC)=O)[C@H](C)[C@@H](O)CH2)=O" etc. But now we have template 1914391 and need to apply to some molecule. The mapped_rxn shows a reaction where product is a complex molecule with a side chain containing P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F etc. The template likely does a substitution of a phosphonate group? The product SMILES in mapped_rxn: "[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13](/[CH:14]=[C:15](/[CH3:16])[C:17](=[O:18])[O:19][CH3:20])[O:21]1". That's the product. The reactants: "C[CH:16](P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)[C:15]#[C:17][O:19][CH3:20]" plus the rest? Actually the mapped_rxn shows left side: "[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13]([CH:14]=[O:18])[O:21]1.C[CH:16](P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)[C:15]#[C:17][O:19][CH3:20]". So two reactants: the core molecule (same as product but with a carbonyl? Actually it's the same core but with a carbonyl at position 14? The product has a double bond to C15 etc). The second reactant is a phosphonate alkyne? "C[CH:16](P(=O)(OCC(F)(F)F)OCC(F)(F)F)[C:15]#[C:17][O:19][CH3:20]" which is a propargyl phosphonate? So applying reverse direction (retro) would break the product into those two precursors.

Thus we need to apply template to the target molecule (product). The product SMILES is the one in mapped_rxn product side. That is: "[CH3][CH2][O][C](=O)[CH2][C@H]1[CH2][C@H]([OH])[C@@H]([CH3])[C@@H](/[CH]=[O])[O]1" but with stereochemistry. Let's get the exact SMILES from mapped_rxn product: "[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13](/[CH:14]=[C:15](/[CH3:16])[C:17](=[O:18])[O:19][CH3:20])[O:21]1". Remove atom mapping and spaces: "CCO C(=O)C[C@H]1CC(O)C(C)C@@H(/C=C(C)C(=O)OCH3)O1"? Wait need to reconstruct.

Let's convert: CH3-CH2-O-C(=O)-CH2- C@H1-CH2- C@H(OH)-C@@H(CH3)-C@@H( /CH:14 = C:15 ( /CH3:16 ) C:17(=O:18) O:19 CH3:20 ) O:21 1.

So product SMILES likely: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1CC(O)C(C)C@@H(/C=C(C)C(=O)OCH3)O1". That matches earlier molecule we tried to apply template to (the same). Indeed earlier we attempted apply_template with that SMILES and got error due to stereochemistry? The error was about AssignStereochemistry on NoneType, maybe the SMILES parsing failed due to some syntax. Let's ensure correct SMILES: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1CC(O)C(C)C@@H(/C=C(C)C(=O)OCH3)O1". Use that.

Let's try apply_template again with correct SMILES.
